'127.0.0.1'`，`--host`/`--port` 照旧能到达它。局域网可达性改为运行时状态：`src/lan-forward.ts` 的转发器在 web server 的实际端口上、按局域网接口监听，并转发到同一端口的 `127.0.0.1`。\n\n栅栏辅助函数（`isTrustedApiRequest` / `isLoopbackHostname`）在 `src/gate.ts` / `src/routes.ts` 本地重实现：connection 插件不再导出它们，配对路由自带一份、只作用于二维码链接宣传的字面量。回环问题在那里被拆成两层：`isLoopbackUpstream`（回环套接字与 Host，刻意忽略转发头）只判断一个 Host 能否被应答，`isLoopbackClient`（无转发头）判断谁能拿到凭据或桌面载荷。`shared/host/loopback.ts` 的共享副本继续让 `isLoopbackRequest` 拒绝一切被转发的请求，并新增 `isForwardedLoopbackRequest`，描述某个路由族可在自己的默认关闭开关之后放行的那个更窄形态。\n\n## 手动 E2E：局域网配对往返\n\n单测/组件 spec 覆盖路由族、栅栏、通道、局域网转发器与其状态帧、适配层，但配对闭环涉及非回环源上的真实浏览器。凡改动 wire 契约或连接循环之后请重跑：\n\n1. 启动隔离实例：`DSH_HOME=/tmp/dsh-qa dsh --profile web --no-open --port 3191`；在 `http://127.0.0.1:3191` 打开卡片、打开**局域网访问**，确认卡片报告转发器已在本机局域网 IPv4 与该端口上监听。\n2. 浏览器打开**回环** URL（`http://127.0.0.1:3191`）：手机图标位于侧栏底部；面板立即铸造二维码，链接形如 `<lan-url>/pair-accept?pair=<token>`。若配置了公网地址，链接改指该源（随处可达），网络选择由落地页完成，见「使用」一节。\n3. 在第二个标签（390x844 触控模拟）打开该链接：链路在 https 源上是 `/pair-accept → /pair-app?grant=<一次性> → /`，在纯 HTTP 局域网上则停在 `/pair-app`；它设置设备 cookie、消费一次性授权、交付打过补丁的官方应用壳并启动 UI——`document.body.classList` 带 `dsh-remote-portrait`、适配样式表与小鲸鱼按钮存在、`__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost` 为 `true`。设置面渲染 host 数据（host 模式），而非 memory 镜像。https 部署下应用壳还会注册重开 service worker（`/pair-app.sw.js`）；在该标签刷新 `/` 会直接进入应用而不是 harness 401。纯 HTTP 局域网下同一个标签刷新 `/pair-app`，同样凭配对 cookie 进入应用。\n4. 桌面徽标实时切换为已连接；局域网源的桌面页面则显示配对面板仅限本机使用横幅且不开状态流。\n5. 桌面点停止切断设备：下一次请求 403 且 `unpaired`（栅栏页提供手动配对令牌输入）。\n\n公网路径是同一条经隧道的往返（见「通过互联网远程访问」）：回环铸造 → 设备打开公网二维码 URL → 接受 → 官方 UI；当对外广告的局域网源确实应答时（`curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<lan-ip>:<port>/pair-ping` 应为 204），落地页会把自身替换为 `http://<lan-ip>:<port>/pair-app?grant=<一次性>`，UI 从局域网源启动。同一会话内再次扫公网二维码会重新落在公网源，因为决定里记着这次没有生效的切换。只有 `publicBaseUrl`（插件配置）命名隧道主机；`--trusted-host` 不属于本配对流。桌面面板仍在 `http://127.0.0.1` 打开。\n\n## 安全模型\n\n- **配对是 `/remote` 通道的访问控制，且无条件生效**：每个请求必须携带有效配对设备 cookie，在任何字节转发之前强制。缺失或被撤销的会话收到 HTTP 403，JSON 拒绝携带 `error.code: \"unpaired\"`；浏览器 `EventSource` API 只暴露流失败，不暴露响应体。该门**不**跟随 `requirePairingForLan`：通道会用进程自身的浏览器认证凭据重新发起每一次调用，放行未配对调用者等于把该权限交出去。局域网策略只作用于普通 `/api` 面，永远不能放宽本通道（issue #1665）。\n- **通道携带进程自己的内部凭据。** harness 浏览器认证 cookie 与 authority 绑定（为浏览器访问过的确切 `host:port` 签发）且没有回环豁免，因此转发到 `127.0.0.1` 的再发起请求无法复用设备的 cookie。插件因此自行兑换一次自己的启动令牌——与浏览器首次访问执行的是同一次交换——并把所得 cookie 附到再发起请求上。该凭据只在上面的配对门之后被使用；停止/取消配对会立即停止对它的使用。\n\n- **通道转发调用者自己的请求头，只把属于本通道的那些留在门外（issue #1925）。** 插件可能用自己的头认证自己的调用——实测命中案例是 `@michengai/dsh-im-connect` 的 `/sessions/ensure` 带 `x-dsh-im-connect-client`——所以再发起的请求不再按固定白名单重建：除本通道自己掌握的头之外全部透传。它把 `host` 改写为回环权威、用进程自己的内层凭据替换调用者 cookie、合成 `sec-fetch-site: same-origin`，并丢弃 `origin`/`referer`、整族浏览器 fetch 元数据（`sec-*`）、逐跳头（含调用者自己在 `Connection` 头里点名的那些）、转发标记（`x-forwarded-*`、`cf-connecting-ip`、`forwarded`、`x-real-ip`——再发起的请求是回环请求，边缘留下的戳会让围栏把它判成远程），以及无 cookie 的设备凭据 `x-dsh-remote-device`：门在入口消费它，绝不向外转发。`accept-encoding`、`range` 与 `if-range` 同样不透传，因为本代理复制的响应头里既没有 `content-encoding` 也没有 `content-range`。\n- **运行时现实：局域网浏览器走 `/remote` 网关，不走原生 `/api`。** 本插件从不重绑 web server，因此宿主停在本机回环上，harness 的 `/api` Host 围栏对局域网权威返回 403。转发器让宿主在局域网上可达，但那里只有本插件自己的面在应答：配对入口页、状态视图与门控 `/remote` 通道。要在局域网权威上恢复原生 `/api`，需要 harness web server 的 `trustedHosts`，这不在本包范围内；运维自己用 `--host` 把宿主绑到网络时，那块面只由 harness 围栏约束，因为官方运行时没有任何组件发出 `api/gate` seam（对照本仓库安装的 0.2.2-rc.1 包核实）。在这种部署下，设备已经兑换过的浏览器凭据在停止/取消配对后仍然有效，直到其自然过期（30 天）——撤销约束的是 `/remote` 通道与配对 cookie，而不是那个凭据。插件会对 `/api` 姿态做探测并大声告警；请把宿主暴露到网络当作深思熟虑的决定，在共享机器上优先回环加隧道。\n- **配对设备是完全控制凭据。** host 模式下它可达完整 host API——聊天、会话、设置、凭据、Agent 预设、产出物——与 SDK 对回环桌面的信任一致。只有三个控制面（配对、自更新、插件安装/卸载）保持物理本地。只配对你控制的设备；停止或逐设备取消配对立即撤销。\n- **控制端点仅限回环，状态视图对隧道访客只答最小载荷**：铸造/停止/撤销/重命名/合并、设备列表、事件流与 lan-bind 状态只应答桌面请求（回环套接字与回环 Host、无转发头），门控通道同时让自更新与插件安装路径保持物理本地。`/api/pair/status` 经隧道可达，但被转发或未配对的调用者只会收到 `{ ok, paired, requirePairingForLan, phase, lanAvailable }`；完整快照——令牌过期时间、公网隧道 URL、计数——与逐设备列表只留在桌面。局域网源浏览器看到「配对面板仅限本机使用」横幅。\n- **带转发头的请求一律视为远程（issue #1906），只有运维本人可以收窄它。** 部署在宿主前面的反向代理——Cloudflare 隧道、frp、nginx 反代——拨的是 `127.0.0.1:<port>` 并把 Host 头改写成该上游字面量，于是源站为一个公网请求同时看到回环套接字与回环 Host：回环判定两半都成立，配对门会直接放行。围栏因此把携带 `CF-Connecting-IP` 或 `X-Forwarded-For` 的请求判为被转发、永不视为本机。该规则只存在一份（`shared/host/loopback.ts` 的 `isProxiedRequest`，由 `isLoopbackRequest` 消费），并随同步副本在全部包生效。本包把这个问题拆成两层（issue #1919）：`isLoopbackUpstream`（回环套接字与 Host，刻意忽略转发头）只判断一个 Host 能否被应答，因此隧道访客能到达配对状态与入口页；`isLoopbackClient`（无转发头）继续守护配对门、`/api/pair` 控制面与桌面载荷。本包没有任何开关会把被转发的请求放进承载凭据的面；同级 task-board 插件把那个更窄的反例做成自己的默认关闭开关（`trustForwardedProxy`）。真实的桌面请求（回环套接字 + 回环 Host + 无转发头）仍判为本机；浏览器同源标记逻辑未改动，跨站请求照旧被拒。残余风险：会剥掉这两个头的代理会让请求重新回到与桌面相同的形状，任何基于头的规则都无法区分——请让代理转发 `X-Forwarded-For`（Cloudflare 与 nginx 默认转发），并注意本机进程本来就能伪造任何请求头。\n- **后台文件上传同样走通道。** 官方上传服务优先使用 Web Worker 载体，其独立全局对象不受主线程补丁影响；因此引导补丁（以及作为兜底的浏览器补丁）会发布官方启动前钩子 `__DSH_FILE_UPLOAD__`，并把打过补丁的 `fetch` 交给它：原始 `/api/session/uploadFileBinary` POST 会被改写到 `/remote`，并像其他受门控调用一样携带设备凭据。没有该钩子时，配对浏览器的上传会绕过通道，被 harness 浏览器认证围栏拒为 401（issue #1580）。该钩子仅在非回环源、且通道安装期间发布，且永不覆盖页面已有的钩子。\n- **落地页 URL 只携带一次性授权，绝不携带设备 ID。** `/pair-accept` 签发 256 位、一次性消费、TTL 60 秒的授权并 303 到 `/pair-app?grant=<g>`；落地页消费它——无论成功、过期还是重放都先删除记录，因此重放或过期的授权解析不出任何设备——再由自己的响应把设备 ID 交给应用壳。设备 ID 是活的会话凭据，因此永不进入 URL、地址栏或重定向路径上的任何日志。请求经 TLS 到达时（`x-forwarded-proto: https`）配对 cookie 带 `Secure`，局域网明文 HTTP Do not edit this copy; edit the shared source and run \"node scripts/sync-shared.mjs\".\n/**\n * Anonymous install telemetry shared by the DSH Web UI family plugins.\n *\n * Once per UTC day per browser, each wired plugin sends one heartbeat to\n * the dsh-market edge API listing its package name (and version when known).\n * The payload carries no conversation data and no identifiers beyond a random\n * UUID generated in localStorage; the server hashes it with a deployment salt\n * before storage and never persists IP addresses. The system is documented in docs/telemetry.md.\n */\n\nexport type TelemetryChannel = 'market' | 'npm' | 'unknown'\n\nexport interface TelemetryItem {\n  /** npm package name or asset id, e.g. \"@linxin666/dsh-pet\" or \"skin:harbor\". */\n  name: string\n  /** Installed version when known; omitted otherwise. */\n  version?: string\n  /** Install channel when determinable (market = Workshop install). */\n  channel?: TelemetryChannel\n}\n\n/** localStorage key carrying the family-wide telemetry opt-out ('1' = off). */\nexport const TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY = 'dsh-web-ui-telemetry-opt-out'\n\nconst VISITOR_KEY = 'dsh-web-ui-telemetry-visitor'\nconst DAY_KEY_PREFIX = 'dsh-web-ui-telemetry-day:'\nconst ENDPOINT = 'https://dsh-market.com/api/telemetry/event'\n\n// Baked into each client bundle by shared/tsdown.client.ts (the package's own\n// package.json version at build time). Undefined in dev/test builds.\ndeclare const __DSH_PKG_VERSION__: string | undefined\n\n/** The building package's version, when the bundle carries it. */\nfunction bakedVersion(): string | undefined {\n  try {\n    return typeof __DSH_PKG_VERSION__ === 'string' && __DSH_PKG_VERSION__ !== ''\n      ? __DSH_PKG_VERSION__\n      : undefined\n  } catch {\n    return undefined\n  }\n}\n\n/** Whether the user switched the family-wide opt-out on (reads storage only). */\nexport function isTelemetryOptedOut(): boolean {\n  try {\n    return localStorage.getItem(TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY) === '1'\n  } catch {\n    // Storage unavailable: there is no stored opt-out to honour.\n    return false\n  }\n}\n\n/** Turn the family-wide opt-out on or off (writing '1' / removing the key); never throws. */\nexport function setTelemetryOptedOut(optedOut: boolean): void {\n  try {\n    if (optedOut) localStorage.setItem(TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY, '1')\n    else localStorage.removeItem(TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY)\n  } catch {\n    // Storage unavailable: the preference cannot be persisted on this machine.\n  }\n}\n\n/** Whether the browser itself asks not to be tracked; a failed read means no signal. */\nfunction doNotTrackRequested(): boolean {\n  try {\n    // '1' per the DNT header spec, 'yes' from older Firefox builds.\n    return navigator.doNotTrack === '1' || navigator.doNotTrack === 'yes'\n  } catch {\n    return false\n  }\n}\n\n/** Whether a heartbeat must be suppressed right now: opt-out stored, or the browser asks not to be tracked. */\nexport function isTelemetrySuppressed(): boolean {\n  return isTelemetryOptedOut() || doNotTrackRequested()\n}\n\n/** Read or lazily create the anonymous visitor id; null when storage is unavailable. */\nfunction visitorId(): string | null {\n  try {\n    const existing = localStorage.getItem(VISITOR_KEY)\n    if (existing && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$/.test(existing)) return existing\n    const fresh = crypto.randomUUID().replaceAll('-', '')\n    localStorage.setItem(VISITOR_KEY, fresh)\n    return fresh\n  } catch {\n    // Storage unavailable (privacy mode, sandboxed frame): report nothing.\n    return null\n  }\n}\n\n/** Drop stale per-day dedup keys so localStorage does not grow forever. */\nfunction pruneDayKeys(today: string): void {\n  try {\n    for (let index = localStorage.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {\n      const key = localStorage.key(index)\n      if (key !== null && key.startsWith(DAY_KEY_PREFIX) && key !== DAY_KEY_PREFIX + today) {\n        localStorage.removeItem(key)\n      }\n    }\n  } catch { /* best effort */ }\n}\n\n/**\n * Fire the daily heartbeat for the given items at most once per UTC day per\n * browser. Never throws and never blocks the caller. Items without an explicit\n * version inherit the bundle's baked build version.\n */\nexport function reportDailyHeartbeat(items: readonly TelemetryItem[]): void {\n  try {\n    // First guard: a stored opt-out or the browser's Do Not Track stops every\n    // read below from minting an id, marking the day, or reaching the network.\n    if (isTelemetrySuppressed()) return\n    if (items.length === 0) return\n    const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)\n    // Automation contexts (CDP-driven QA browsers, fresh isolated profiles)\n    // mint a new visitor id per run and would inflate instance counts.\n    if (navigator.webdriver) return\n    if (localStorage.getItem(DAY_KEY_PREFIX + today) !== null) return\n    const visitor = visitorId()\n    if (visitor === null) return\n    pruneDayKeys(today)\n    const payloadItems = items.map((item) => {\n      const out: Record<string, string> = { name: item.name }\n      const version = item.version ?? bakedVersion()\n      if (version !== undefined) out.version = version\n      if (item.channel !== undefined) out.channel = item.channel\n      return out\n    })\n    const body = JSON.stringify({ kind: 'heartbeat', visitor, items: payloadItems })\n    void fetch(ENDPOINT, {\n      method: 'POST',\n      headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\n      body,\n      keepalive: true,\n    }).then((response) => {\n      // Mark the day only after an accepted send, so offline browsers retry\n      // on a later mount instead of going dark until tomorrow.\n      if (response.ok) localStorage.setItem(DAY_KEY_PREFIX + today, '1')\n    }).catch(() => { /* unreachable endpoint: stay silent */ })\n  } catch { /* never break the host UI over telemetry */ }\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * The `api/gate` listener: application-level access control layered on top\n * of the transport fence (the fence is Host/Origin based and explicitly not\n * an authentication layer — packages/client/connection documents this\n * event as the sanctioned seam for pairing/revocation).\n *\n * Policy: loopback requests (the desktop) pass without a device identity;\n * every non-loopback /api request must carry a live, non-revoked device\n * cookie — intended to make the QR the only way into a LAN-exposed dsh web\n * and to give \"停止\" real teeth for direct /api callers.\n *\n * Cohort reality (0.1.2-alpha.2): NOTHING emits api/gate in the official\n * runtime, so this listener never fires there and direct /api is governed\n * solely by the harness fence + browser-auth cookie. The pairing gate with\n * real teeth lives on the plugin's own /remote channel (remote-api.ts); the\n * listener stays wired for cohort lines that do carry the seam, and the\n * README security model states the gap plainly.\n */\n\nimport type { IncomingMessage } from 'node:http'\nimport type { PairingService } from './pairing.ts'\nimport { isLoopbackAddress, isLoopbackHostname, isProxiedRequest } from './loopback.ts'\n\n/**\n * Read one cookie value from a Cookie header.\n * @param header - the raw Cookie header value (or undefined).\n * @param name - the cookie name.\n * @returns the value, or undefined when absent.\n */\nexport function readCookie(header: string | undefined, name: string): string | undefined {\n  if (header === undefined) return undefined\n  for (const part of header.split(';')) {\n    const eq = part.indexOf('=')\n    if (eq < 0) continue\n    const key = part.slice(0, eq).trim()\n    if (key === name) return part.slice(eq + 1).trim()\n  }\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * The effective Host hostname of a request.\n * @param request - node HTTP request.\n * @returns the normalized hostname, or undefined when unparsable.\n */\nexport function hostnameOf(request: IncomingMessage): string | undefined {\n  const host = request.headers.host\n  if (typeof host !== 'string') return undefined\n  try {\n    return new URL(`http://${host}`).hostname\n  } catch {\n    return undefined\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether the request arrived at this process over a loopback upstream: a\n * loopback socket and a loopback Host header, with the forwarding headers\n * deliberately ignored. A reverse proxy (a Cloudflare tunnel, frp, nginx) dials\n * 127.0.0.1:<port> and rewrites the Host to that upstream literal, so this is\n * the shape of a tunneled request as much as of the desktop one.\n *\n * It answers \"this process is reachable at a loopback authority\", never \"this\n * request is the desktop\": the desktop decision is {@link isLoopbackClient},\n * which a forwarded request never satisfies. Only the fences that decide whether\n * a Host is answerable at all (the pairing status view, the reachability beacon,\n * the pairing entry pages) may be built on this predicate; every decision that\n * hands out a credential or the desktop payload stays on {@link isLoopbackClient}\n * (issue #1919 keeps #1906 shut: reachability for the visitor, payload and\n * control plane for the desktop).\n * @param request - node HTTP request.\n * @returns true when the socket and the Host both name loopback.\n */\nexport function isLoopbackUpstream(request: IncomingMessage): boolean {\n  const hostname = hostnameOf(request)\n  if (hostname === undefined || !isLoopbackHostname(hostname)) return false\n  const socket = request.socket as { remoteAddress?: string } | undefined\n  return isLoopbackAddress(socket?.remoteAddress)\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether a request comes from the desktop loopback client: a loopback upstream\n * ({@link isLoopbackUpstream}) reached with no forwarding header. This is the\n * same decision the shared copy makes in `isLoopbackRequest` (sans the browser\n * same-origin markers, which the /api/pair routes apply separately through\n * `isTrustedApiRequest`), and it carries the same proxy rule: a reverse proxy\n * rewrites the Host to its own 127.0.0.1:<port> upstream and connects over\n * loopback, so a request that arrives with CF-Connecting-IP or X-Forwarded-For\n * is a forwarded one and is never the desktop (issue #1906). Every decision\n * that grants the desktop payload or a control plane (the api/gate listener,\n * the events stream, /api/pair/issue, /api/pair/stop, /api/pair/revoke,\n * /api/pair/lan-bind) reads this predicate, so the rule holds for all of them.\n * @param request - node HTTP request.\n * @returns true for a local desktop request with no proxy in front of it.\n */\nexport function isLoopbackClient(request: IncomingMessage): boolean {\n  if (isProxiedRequest(request)) return false\n  return isLoopbackUpstream(request)\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the api/gate listener for one pairing service.\n * @param service - the pairing service.\n * @param requirePairingForLan - when false, non-loopback requests pass\n * without a device cookie (the feature then only manages tokens/status;\n * revocation of paired devices still holds). A function is re-read per\n * request, so a settings edit takes effect without a restart. Defaults to true.\n * @param enabled - when false, every non-loopback request is vetoed while\n * loopback stays available. A function is re-read per request so the fence\n * stays mounted for the plugin lifetime and disabling the plugin cannot open\n * a LAN-exposed /api. Defaults to true.\n * @returns the cordis waterfall listener: call `next()` to delegate,\n * return false (without calling it) to veto with 403.\n */\nexport function makeGateListener(\n  service: PairingService,\n  requirePairingForLan: boolean | (() => boolean) = true,\n  enabled: boolean | (() => boolean) = true,\n): (request: IncomingMessage, method: string | undefined, next: () => boolean | Promise<boolean>) => boolean | Promise<boolean> {\n  return (request, _method, next) => {\n    // Loopback clients (desktop at 127.0.0.1) always pass without cookie check.\n    if (isLoopbackClient(request)) return next()\n    const active = typeof enabled === 'function' ? enabled() : enabled\n    if (!active) return false\n    const require = typeof requirePairingForLan === 'function' ? requirePairingForLan() : requirePairingForLan\n    // When pairing is not required for LAN, non-loopback requests pass too.\n    if (!require) return next()\n    // Non-loopback origin: verify paired-device cookie. A recompose\n    // pass can run this apply before the listener binds: defer the tunnel\n    // branch (and re-plan on a short timer) instead of minting an\n    // http://127.0.0.1:undefined target; everything else in sync applies.\n    // Read through the normalizer: a half-read webServer can hand NaN/Infinity,\n    // and that must take the unbound-port path (settle retry, no request) rather\n    // than mint a \":NaN\" target or leave every dependent surface waiting.\n    const livePort = livePortOf(ctx.webServer.port)\n    const tunnelNeedsPort = livePort === undefined && value.autoTunnel === true\n    if (tunnelNeedsPort) {\n      if (!portSettleWarned) {\n        portSettleWarned = true\n        console.warn('remote-web-ui: autoTunnel is on but the web server port is not bound yet — the quick tunnel starts once the port settles')\n      }\n      schedulePortSettleRetry()\n    } else {\n      portSettleWarned = false\n      applyTunnelPlan(value, livePort)\n    }\n    // The ingress sync learns the live port in both branches: an unbound\n    // listener is a zero-request wait there, and the same settle timer delivers\n    // the port — no second retry loop of its own.\n    scheduleIngressSync(value, livePort)\n    if (livePort === undefined && !tunnelNeedsPort && value.ingressSync === true) schedulePortSettleRetry()\n    // The lease and the bridge are transport-owned, not tunnel-owned: a\n    // bridge-mode instance has to reach its object even when no quick tunnel\n    // runs (the claim is the only answer that carries the bridge grant, and\n    // without it the edge reports no-connector forever). The dedupe key keeps\n    // a settings sync from re-claiming, and a fresh quick URL re-claims.\n    if (value.enabled && value.relay !== false) {\n      if (livePort === undefined) schedulePortSettleRetry()\n      else claimRelayLeaseFor(livePort, publicBase.quickUrl())\n    }\n    const enabled = value.enabled\n    if (!enabled) {\n      service.stop()\n      // The tunnel branch above follows the plan, not the master switch, so an\n      // explicit \"off\" must also drop the public ingress it started: otherwise\n      // the cloudflared child keeps a live public URL (and the relay keeps its\n      // stable row) while the panel says remote control is stopped.       "path": "packages/dsh-remote-web-ui/src/inner-auth.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * The inner browser credential for the remote desktop channel. The proxied\n * /api re-issues requests to 127.0.0.1, where the connection plugin's route\n * enforces the harness browser-auth cookie — an authority-bound signed cookie\n * with no loopback exemption on this cohort line, so a cookie minted for the\n * device's own authority can never satisfy the inner check. The process\n * therefore redeems its own launch token (the same one-time exchange every\n * paired device's first navigation performs) and attaches the resulting\n * cookie to inner requests. The credential is only ever exercised behind the\n * pairing gate: the `/remote` channel always requires a live paired-device\n * credential before this module is consulted, regardless of the\n * requirePairingForLan LAN policy (issue #1665).\n */\n\n/** Browser-auth credential the proxy attaches to loopback-bound requests. */\nexport interface InnerAuth {\n  /**\n   * Resolve the `name=value` cookie pair for inner requests, or undefined\n   * when the launch token is unavailable (the proxy then sends without a\n   * credential and the inner route answers 401, exactly as before).\n   */\n  ready(): Promise<string | undefined>\n  /** Drop the cached credential; the next ready() re-redeems. */\n  invalidate(): void\n}\n\n/** The harness browser-auth cookie name prefix (see dsh-client-connection). */\nconst BROWSER_AUTH_COOKIE_PREFIX = 'dsh-auth-'\n\n/**\n * Build the inner-auth handle.\n * @param launchUrl - the launch-token URL for the inner loopback authority\n *   (the connection service's authenticatedUrl of `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`),\n *   or undefined when the connection service or port is unavailable.\n * @param fetchImpl - injectable fetch (tests).\n */\nexport function createInnerAuth(\n  launchUrl: () => string | undefined,\n  fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch,\n): InnerAuth {\n  let cached: string | undefined\n  let inflight: Promise<string | undefined> | undefined\n\n  const redeem = async (): Promise<string | undefined> => {\n    const url = launchUrl()\n    if (url === undefined) return undefined\n    try {\n      // redirect: 'manual' keeps the 303's set-cookie readable instead of\n      // following it; the exchange itself is a plain GET with the token in\n      // the query, exactly what a first browser visit performs.\n      const response = await fetchImpl(url, { redirect: 'manual' })\n      const raw = response.headers.get('set-cookie')\n      if (raw === null) return undefined\n      // Generated cookie values are base64url and never contain commas, so a\n      // comma split followed by a prefix match finds the browser-auth entry\n      // even when the exchange sets several cookies.\n      const entry = raw\n        .split(',')\n        .map((part) => part.trim())\n        .find((part) => part.startsWith(BROWSER_AUTH_COOKIE_PREFIX))\n      if (entry === undefined) return undefined\n      const pair = entry.split(';')[0]?.trim()\n      return pair !== undefined && pair.includes('=') ? pair : undefined\n    } catch {\n      return undefined\n    }\n  }\n\n  return {\n    ready(): Promise<string | undefined> {\n      if (cached !== undefined) return Promise.resolve(cached)\n      inflight ??= redeem().then((value) => {\n        if (value !== undefined) cached = value\n        inflight = undefined\n        return value\n      }, () => {\n        inflight = undefined\n        return undefined\n      })\n      return inflight\n    },\n    invalidate(): void {\n      cached = undefined\n    },\n  }\n}\n"

      "path": "packages/dsh-remote-web-ui/src/lan-forward.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * The LAN edge the lan-bind toggle owns (issue #1917).\n *\n * The toggle used to pin the LAN address into the profile's webserver row. That\n * row is the only place the harness takes its bind from, and rewriting it\n *   - replaced the official row's whole config (so the row's own\n *     `host: !!js ctx.webStartup.host ?? '127.0.0.1'` expression and the CLI\n *     `--host`/`--port` never reached it), and\n *   - the profile patch is watched by the Host's HMR config watcher, so the\n *     write recomposed the running process and rebound the live listener.\n *\n * This module keeps the host bound to loopback and gives LAN clients their own\n * listener: a forwarder on the machine's LAN address, on the same port, that\n * re-issues every request (HTTP and WebSocket upgrade alike) to\n * `127.0.0.1:<port>`. Two consequences are load-bearing:\n *\n * 1. The upstream leg is loopback, so the socket alone would read as \"the\n *    desktop\". The forwarder therefore DROPS whatever Host the client sent and\n *    stamps the LAN authority it was reached at, plus `X-Forwarded-For`. Every\n *    fence that decides \"is this the desktop\" (`isLoopbackClient`, the pairing\n *    gate, the `/remote` gate) then keeps refusing the forwarded request, while\n *    the phone-facing fences still match the LAN authority the QR advertises.\n * 2. A bind that cannot be taken (address gone after a network change, port\n *    taken) only loses the LAN edge: the loopback listener is never touched, so\n *    the host cannot be bricked and the failure is reported on the status\n *    frame.\n *\n * Nothing here writes a file: the forwarder is runtime state, so a network\n * change needs no profile edit and no restart.\n *\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui/lan-forward\n */\n\nimport { createServer, request as httpRequest, type ClientRequest, type IncomingMessage, type Server, type ServerResponse } from 'node:http'\nimport { connect } from 'node:net'\nimport type { Duplex } from 'node:stream'\n\n/** The upstream the forwarder re-issues to: the process's own loopback listener. */\nexport const FORWARD_UPSTREAM_HOST = '127.0.0.1'\n\n/**\n * Headers that describe one hop rather than the request. They are rebuilt for\n * each leg so a keep-alive or upgrade marker from the client never leaks into\n * the loopback leg (and vice versa on the response).\n */\nconst HOP_BY_HOP = new Set([\n  'connection',\n  'keep-alive',\n  'proxy-authenticate',\n  'proxy-authorization',\n  'proxy-connection',\n  'te',\n  'trailer',\n  'transfer-encoding',\n  'upgrade',\n])\n\n/**\n * Headers the forwarder owns: a client-supplied value is discarded, never\n * appended to, so a LAN client cannot claim to be the desktop by forging them.\n */\nconst REWRITTEN = new Set(['host', 'x-forwarded-for', 'x-forwarded-proto', 'x-forwarded-host', 'cf-connecting-ip'])\n\n/** What the forwarder is doing right now, for the status frame and the logs. */\nexport interface LanForwardState {\n  /** Whether the LAN listener is bound. */\n  listening: boolean\n  /** The LAN address it listens on (undefined when it never bound). */\n  address: string | undefined\n  /** The port it listens on (the web server's own port). */\n  port: number | undefined\n  /** The loopback port it re-issues to. */\n  upstreamPort: number | undefined\n  /** Why the last bind attempt failed, when it did. */\n  error: string | undefined\n}\n\n/** The idle state: nothing bound, nothing failed. */\nexport const IDLE_FORWARD_STATE: LanForwardState = {\n  listening: false,\n  address: undefined,\n  port: undefined,\n  upstreamPort: undefined,\n  error: undefined,\n}\n\n/**\n * The `Host` authority a listener at `address:port` is reached at. IPv6\n * literals are bracketed like any URL authority.\n * @param address - the listen address (a literal).\n * @param port - the listen port.\n * @returns the authority text a request to that listener carries.\n */\nexport function authorityOf(address: string, port: number): string {\n  const host = address.includes(':') ? `[${address}]` : address\n  return `${host}:${String(port)}`\n}\n\n/**\n * The headers the loopback leg carries for one request: the client's own\n * headers minus the hop-by-hop and forwarder-owned ones, plus the LAN authority\n * the client actually reached and its address.\n * @param request - the request as it arrived on the LAN listener.\n * @param authority - the LAN authority the forwarder listens at.\n * @param clientAddress - the client's socket address, when readable.\n * @returns the headers for the loopback request.\n */\nexport function forwardedHeaders(\n  request: IncomingMessage,\n  authority: string,\n  clientAddress: string | undefined,\n): Record<string, string> {\n  const headers: Record<string, string> = {}\n  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(request.headers)) {\n    if (value === undefined) continue\n    const lower = name.toLowerCase()\n    if (HOP_BY_HOP.has(lower) || REWRITTEN.has(lower)) continue\n    headers[lower] = Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : value\n  }\n  headers.host = authority\n  if (clientAddress !== undefined && clientAddress !== '') headers['x-forwarded-for'] = clientAddress\n  headers['x-forwarded-proto'] = 'http'\n  return headers\n}\n\n/**\n * Rebuild a WebSocket handshake for the loopback leg. The client's own headers\n * travel through verbatim (so `Sec-WebSocket-*` and any application protocol\n * survive) except the ones the forwarder owns.\n * @param request - the upgrade request as it arrived on the LAN listener.\n * @param authority - the LAN authority the forwarder listens at.\n * @param clientAddress - the client's socket address, when readable.\n * @returns the handshake request head to write on the loopback leg.\n */\nexport function forwardedHandshake(\n  request: IncomingMessage,\n  authority: string,\n  clientAddress: string | undefined,\n): string {\n  const lines = [`${request.method ?? 'GET'} ${request.url ?? '/'} HTTP/1.1`]\n  const raw = request.rawHeaders\n  for (let index = 0; index + 1 < raw.length; index += 2) {\n    const name = raw[index] ?? ''\n    const lower = name.toLowerCase()\n    if (REWRITTEN.has(lower)) continue\n    lines.push(`${name}: ${raw[index + 1] ?? ''}`)\n  }\n  lines.push(`Host: ${authority}`)\n  if (clientAddress !== undefined && clientAddress !== '') lines.push(`X-Forwarded-For: ${clientAddress}`)\n  lines.push('X-Forwarded-Proto: http')\n  return `${lines.join('\\r\\n')}\\r\\n\\r\\n`\n}\n\n/** One listener, its live connections, and its last bind outcome. */\nexport class LanForwarder {\n  private server: Server | undefined\n  private config: { address: string; port: number; upstreamPort: number } | undefined\n  private state: LanForwardState = IDLE_FORWARD_STATE\n  /** Every socket this forwarder opened on either leg. */\n  private readonly sockets = new Set<Duplex>()\n  /** Every in-flight loopback request, so a teardown cannot leave one running. */\n  private readonly upstreams = new Set<ClientRequest>()\n\n  /** What the forwarder is doing right now. */\n  snapshot(): LanForwardState {\n    return this.state\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Bind the LAN listener, or report why it could not be bound.\n   *\n   * Never throws: a bind failure is the ordinary outcome after a network change\n   * (the address is gone) or a port collision, and the loopback listener must\n   * keep serving regardless.\n   * @param address - the LAN address to listen on.\n   * @param port - the port to listen on (the web server's own port).\n   * @param upstreamPort - the loopback port to re-issue to; defaults to `port`.\n   * @returns the settled state.\n   */\n  start(address: string, port: number, upstreamPort: number = port): Promise<LanForwardState> {\n    if (this.config !== undefined && this.state.listening\n      && this.config.address === address && this.config.port === port && this.config.upstreamPort === upstreamPort) {\n      return Promise.resolve(this.state)\n    }\n    return this.stop().then(() => this.bind(address, port, upstreamPort))\n  }\n\n  private bind(address: string, port: number, upstreamPort: number): Promise<LanForwardState> {\n    // The authority the requests are stamped with; re-read after listen so a\n    // kernel-assigned port (or a resolved address) is what clients are told.\n    let authority = authorityOf(address, port)\n    const server = createServer((request, response) => { this.forwardHttp(request, response, upstreamPort, authority) })\n    server.on('upgrade', (request, socket, head) => { this.forwardUpgrade(request, socket, head, upstreamPort, authority) })\n    server.on('connection', (socket) => {\n      this.sockets.add(socket)\n      socket.on('close', () => { this.sockets.delete(socket) })\n    })\n    this.server = server\n    this.config = { address, port, upstreamPort }\n    return new Promise<LanForwardState>((resolve) => {\n      let settled = false\n      const settle = (next: LanForwardState): void => {\n        if (settled) return\n        settled = true\n        this.state = next\n        resolve(next)\n      }\n      // A failed bind arrives as an 'error' event (EADDRINUSE, EADDRNOTAVAIL, a\n      // permission refusal). It is reported, never re-thrown: an unhandled\n      // 'error' on a listening server would take the whole host process down.\n      server.on('error', (error: NodeJS.ErrnoException) => {\n        const reason = error.code === undefined ? error.message : `${error.code}: ${error.message}`\n        if (this.server === server) {\n          this.server = undefined\n          this.config = undefined\n        }\n        this.releaseSockets()\n        settle({ listening: false, address, port, upstreamPort, error: reason })\n        if (!server.listening) return\n        server.close(() => undefined)\n      })\n      server.listen(port, address, () => {\n        // Report the address and port the kernel actually bound: a port of 0\n        // (and a wildcard-adjacent literal) is resolved by the listen call, and\n        // the status frame must name the listener clients can dial.\n        const bound = server.address()\n        const boundPort = typeof bound === 'object' && bound !== null ? bound.port : port\n        const boundAddress = typeof bound === 'object' && bound !== null ? bound.address : address\n        authority = authorityOf(boundAddress, boundPort)\n        this.config = { address: boundAddress, port: boundPort, upstreamPort }\n        settle({ listening: true, address: boundAddress, port: boundPort, upstreamPort, error: undefined })\n      })\n    })\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Close the LAN listener and every connection it opened, then resolve once the\n   * port is released. Safe to call when nothing is bound.\n   */\n  stop(): Promise<void> {\n    const server = this.server\n    this.server = undefined\n    this.config = undefined\n    this.releaseSockets()\n    this.state = IDLE_FORWARD_STATE\n    if (server === undefined) return Promise.resolve()\n    return new Promise<void>((resolve) => {\n      server.close(() => { resolve() })\n      // Keep-alive and upgraded connections keep the handle alive; they are\n      // already destroyed above, so the close above settles on the next tick.\n      server.closeAllConnections?.()\n    })\n  }\n\n  private releaseSockets(): void {\n    for (const upstream of this.upstreams) upstream.destroy()\n    this.upstreams.clear()\n    for (const socket of this.sockets) socket.destroy()\n    this.sockets.clear()\n  }\n\n  private trackUpstream(upstream: ClientRequest): void {\n    this.upstreams.add(upstream)\n    upstream.on('close', () => { this.upstreams.delete(upstream) })\n  }\n\n  private forwardHttp(request: IncomingMessage, response: ServerResponse, upstreamPort: number, authority: string): void {\n    const upstream = httpRequest({\n      host: FORWARD_UPSTREAM_HOST,\n      port: upstreamPort,\n      method: request.method,\n      path: request.url,\n      headers: forwardedHeaders(request, authority, request.socket.remoteAddress),\n    }, (upstreamResponse) => {\n      const headers: Record<string, string | string[]> = {}\n      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(upstreamResponse.headers)) {\n        if (value === undefined || HOP_BY_HOP.has(name.toLowerCase())) continue\n        headers[name] = value\n      }\n      response.writeHead(upstreamResponse.statusCode ?? 502, headers)\n      upstreamResponse.pipe(response)\n      upstreamResponse.on('error', () => { response.destroy() })\n      // The client left mid-response: stop the loopback leg instead of working\n      // on a call nobody will read.\n      response.on('close', () => {\n        if (!upstreamResponse.readableEnded) upstream.destroy()\n      })\n    })\n    this.trackUpstream(upstream)\n    upstream.on('error', () => {\n      if (response.headersSent) {\n        response.destroy()\n        return\n      }\n      response.writeHead(502, { 'content-type': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8' })\n      response.end('remote-web-ui: the LAN forwarder could not reach the loopback listener\\n')\n    })\n    request.on('error', () => { upstream.destroy() })\n    request.pipe(upstream)\n  }\n\n  private forwardUpgrade(request: IncomingMessage, socket: Duplex, head: Buffer, upstreamPort: number, authority: string): void {\n    const upstream = connect(upstreamPort, FORWARD_UPSTREAM_HOST)\n    this.sockets.add(upstream)\n    const tearDown = (): void => {\n      this.sockets.delete(upstream)\n      upstream.destroy()\n      socket.destroy()\n    }\n    upstream.on('error', tearDown)\n    socket.on('error', tearDown)\n    upstream.on('close', () => { socket.destroy() })\n    socket.on('close', () => { upstream.destroy() })\n    upstream.on('connect', () => {\n      upstream.write(forwardedHandshake(request, authority, request.socket.remoteAddress))\n      if (head.length > 0) upstream.write(head)\n      socket.pipe(upstream)\n      upstream.pipe(socket)\n    })\n  }\n}\n"

      "path": "packages/dsh-remote-web-ui/src/loopback-proxy.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Loopback-shaped reverse proxy used by the remote desktop channel: after\n * the pairing cookie gate, traffic is re-issued to 127.0.0.1 so sibling\n * plugin fences (socket + Host loopback) accept it. Origin, cookies, and\n * caller-controlled Sec-Fetch markers are dropped, and HTTP requests receive\n * a synthetic same-origin marker so sibling loopback routes that require a\n * browser tripwire accept the authenticated proxy.\n *\n * Every other request header is forwarded unchanged, because a plugin may\n * authenticate its own calls with a header of its own: an allowlist here\n * silently dropped those markers and made the plugin refuse every remote\n * write request (issue #1925).\n */\n\nimport type { IncomingMessage, OutgoingHttpHeaders, ServerResponse } from 'node:http'\nimport { request as httpRequest } from 'node:http'\nimport { connect } from 'node:net'\nimport type { Duplex } from 'node:stream'\nimport { writeJson } from './http.ts'\nimport type { InnerAuth } from './inner-auth.ts'\n\n/** WebSocket handshake headers forwarded to the loopback upstream. */\nconst WS_FORWARD_HEADERS = [\n  'sec-websocket-key',\n  'sec-websocket-version',\n  'sec-websocket-extensions',\n  'sec-websocket-protocol',\n] as const\n\n/**\n * Request headers the re-issue never carries: hop-by-hop headers (RFC 9110\n * 7.6.1), the ones this proxy owns or rewrites, the forwarding marks of a hop\n * that stood in between, and the browser fetch metadata that describes the\n * caller's own request. Everything else is passed through, so a plugin that\n * authenticates its calls with a header of its own keeps working behind the\n * pairing gate (issue #1925).\n *\n * The forwarding marks (x-forwarded-*, cf-connecting-ip, forwarded) must not\n * ride along: the re-issued request is a loopback one, and an edge stamp would\n * make the local fences classify it as remote and refuse every route\n * (shared/host/loopback.ts owns that rule). x-dsh-remote-device is the\n * caller's own live device credential: the channel consumes it at its gate and\n * never hands it further, the same way the WS query parameter is stripped.\n * accept-encoding, range and if-range stay out because the response headers\n * copied below carry neither content-encoding nor content-range, so an invited\n * compressed or partial body could never be described to the caller.\n */\nconst REQUEST_HEADER_DENYLIST = new Set([\n  // hop-by-hop\n  'connection',\n  'keep-alive',\n  'proxy-authenticate',\n  'proxy-authorization',\n  'expect',\n  'te',\n  'trailer',\n  'transfer-encoding',\n  'upgrade',\n  // rewritten by this proxy: the loopback authority and the tripwire marker\n  'host',\n  'sec-fetch-site',\n  // the caller's own origin, its cookie jar, and the credential the gate consumed\n  'origin',\n  'referer',\n  'cookie',\n  'x-dsh-remote-device',\n  // forwarding marks: a re-issued request is loopback, not forwarded\n  'forwarded',\n  'x-forwarded-for',\n  'x-forwarded-host',\n  'x-forwarded-port',\n  'x-forwarded-proto',\n  'x-real-ip',\n  'cf-connecting-ip',\n  // response shaping (see the doc comment above): these ask the upstream for a\n  // body the copied response headers cannot describe\n  'accept-encoding',\n  'range',\n  'if-range',\n])\n\n/**\n * Prefixes the re-issue never carries: the browser fetch metadata\n * (sec-fetch-*, sec-ch-*) describes the outer request, not this one.\n */\nconst REQUEST_HEADER_DENY_PREFIXES = ['sec-']\n\n/**\n * Header names the caller nominated as hop-by-hop through its own Connection\n * header (RFC 9110 7.6.1): whatever it names stops at this proxy too.\n * @param connection - the outer request Connection header value.\n * @returns the nominated names, lowercased.\n */\nfunction nominatedHeaders(connection: string | string[] | undefined): Set<string> {\n  const nominated = new Set<string>()\n  if (connection === undefined) return nominated\n  for (const value of Array.isArray(connection) ? connection : [connection]) {\n    for (const token of value.split(',')) {\n      const name = token.trim().toLowerCase()\n      if (name !== '') nominated.add(name)\n    }\n  }\n  return nominated\n}\n\n/**\n * Headers of the loopback re-issue: the caller headers minus the ones the\n * channel owns, plus the rewritten authority, the synthetic same-origin\n * tripwire, and the inner credential that replaces the caller cookie.\n * @param req - the already-gated outer request.\n * @param port - local webServer port.\n * @param cookie - the inner credential, when one resolved.\n * @returns headers to send to 127.0.0.1.\n */\nfunction forwardedRequestHeaders(req: IncomingMessage, port: number, cookie: string | undefined): Record<string, string> {\n  const nominated = nominatedHeaders(req.headers.connection)\n  const headers: Record<string, string> = {}\n  for (let index = 0; index + 1 < req.rawHeaders.length; index += 2) {\n    const name = req.rawHeaders[index].toLowerCase()\n    if (REQUEST_HEADER_DENYLIST.has(name) || nominated.has(name)) continue\n    if (REQUEST_HEADER_DENY_PREFIXES.some(prefix => name.startsWith(prefix))) continue\n    const value = req.rawHeaders[index + 1]\n    const previous = headers[name]\n    // Repeated headers reach the upstream as one comma-joined value, the same\n    // way node folds duplicates on the receiving side.\n    headers[name] = previous === undefined ? value : `${previous}, ${value}`\n  }\n  headers.host = `127.0.0.1:${String(port)}`\n  headers['sec-fetch-site'] = 'same-origin'\n  if (cookie !== undefined) headers.cookie = cookie\n  return headers\n}\n\n/** Response headers copied from the loopback upstream (no hop-by-hop). */\nconst HTTP_FORWARD_RESPONSE_HEADERS = [\n  'content-type',\n  'content-length',\n  'content-disposition',\n  'cache-control',\n  'etag',\n  'last-modified',\n] as const\n\n/**\n * Pipe one HTTP request to loopback and stream the response back.\n * @param req - the already-gated outer request.\n * @param res - the outer response.\n * @param port - local webServer port.\n * @param upstreamPath - path + query on 127.0.0.1 (must start with `/`).\n * @param auth - when given, the process's inner browser-auth credential is\n *   attached so the connection plugin's /api route (fence + browser auth,\n *   authority-bound cookie, no loopback exemption on this cohort) accepts\n *   the re-issued request; a 401 answer invalidates the cached credential.\n */\nexport function proxyLoopbackHttp(\n  req: IncomingMessage,\n  res: ServerResponse,\n  port: number,\n  upstreamPath: string,\n  auth?: InnerAuth,\n): void {\n  void Promise.resolve(auth?.ready())\n    .catch(() => undefined)\n    .then((cookie) => { pipeLoopbackHttp(req, res, port, upstreamPath, auth, typeof cookie === 'string' ? cookie : undefined) })\n}\n\nfunction pipeLoopbackHttp(\n  req: IncomingMessage,\n  res: ServerResponse,\n  port: number,\n  upstreamPath: string,\n  auth: InnerAuth | undefined,\n  cookie: string | undefined,\n): void {\n  const headers = forwardedRequestHeaders(req, port, cookie)\n\n  const upstream = httpRequest({\n    host: '127.0.0.1',\n    port,\n    path: upstreamPath,\n    method: req.method,\n    headers,\n  }, (upstreamRes) => {\n    // The cached credential went stale (secret rotation, credential store\n    // reset): drop it so the next request re-redeems. The in-flight response\n    // still pipes through untouched.\n    if (upstreamRes.statusCode === 401 && cookie !== undefined) auth?.invalidate()\n    const out: OutgoingHttpHeaders = {}\n    for (const name of HTTP_FORWARD_RESPONSE_HEADERS) {\n      const value = upstreamRes.headers[name]\n      if (value !== undefined) out[name] = value\n    }\n    res.writeHead(upstreamRes.statusCode ?? 502, out)\n    upstreamRes.pipe(res)\n    // Inner leg died mid-response (reset, truncation): tear the outer leg\n    // down instead of letting the truncated response raise an unhandled\n    // 'error' with no listener.\n    upstreamRes.on('error', () => { res.destroy() })\n    // Outer leg died before the response finished (phone left mid-request):\n    // reset the inner request so the loopback server stops working on a call\n    // nobody will read. Guarded so a normal completion never destroys a\n    // keep-alive socket the agent would reuse.\n    res.on('close', () => {\n      if (!upstreamRes.readableEnded) upstream.destroy()\n    })\n  })\n  upstream.on('error', () => {\n    if (!res.headersSent) {\n      writeJson(res, 502, { ok: false, error: { code: 'upstream-failure', message: 'upstream request failed' } })\n      return\n    }\n    res.destroy()\n  })\n  // The outer request aborted mid-body: reset the inner request instead of\n  // feeding it a truncated body that still gets processed (mirror of the\n  // upgrade path's two-leg teardown).\n  req.on('error', () => { upstream.destroy() })\n  req.pipe(upstream)\n}\n\n/**\n * Rebuild a WebSocket handshake as loopback-shaped and pipe both directions.\n * @param req - the already-gated upgrade request.\n * @param socket - the client duplex.\n * @param head - bytes already read past the handshake.\n * @param port - local webServer port.\n * @param upstreamPath - path + query on 127.0.0.1.\n * @param cookie - the inner browser-auth credential for the handshake, when\n *   the upstream route enforces it (the gateway event-stream mux does).\n */\nexport function proxyLoopbackUpgrade(\n  req: IncomingMessage,\n  socket: Duplex,\n  head: Buffer,\n  port: number,\n  upstreamPath: string,\n  cookie?: string,\n): void {\n  const lines = [\n    `GET ${upstreamPath} HTTP/1.1`,\n    `Host: 127.0.0.1:${String(port)}`,\n    'Upgrade: websocket',\n    'Connection: Upgrade',\n  ]\n  if (cookie !== undefined) lines.push(`Cookie: ${cookie}`)\n  for (const name of WS_FORWARD_HEADERS) {\n    const value = req.headers[name]\n    if (value === undefined) continue\n    lines.push(`${name}: ${Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : value}`)\n  }\n  const handshake = `${lines.join('\\r\\n')}\\r\\n\\r\\n`\n\n  const upstream = connect(port, '127.0.0.1')\n  // A half-open tunnel path (dead-but-alive edge connection) would otherwise\n  // let the phone's mux socket sit stale for minutes: keepalive probes the\n  // pipe periodically and destroys both legs on the first real gap, so the\n  // client's reconnect + stream re-baseline re-syncs the feed in seconds.\n  ;(socket as unknown as import('node:net').Socket).setKeepAlive(true, 20_000)\n  upstream.setKeepAlive(true, 20_000)\n  const tearDown = (): void => {\n    upstream.destroy()\n    socket.destroy()\n  }\n  upstream.on('error', tearDown)\n  socket.on('error', tearDown)\n  upstream.on('close', () => { socket.destroy() })\n  socket.on('close', () => { upstream.destroy() })\n  upstream.on('connect', () => {\n    upstream.write(handshake)\n    if (head.length > 0) upstream.write(head)\n    socket.pipe(upstream)\n    upstream.pipe(socket)\n  })\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "packages/dsh-remote-web-ui/src/pair-grant.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * One-time pairing grants for the /pair-app landing.\n *\n * The QR entry (`/pair-accept?pair=<token>`) used to hand the freshly minted\n * device id to the app landing in its own URL (`/pair-app?device=<id>`). A\n * device id is a live session credential: the channel gate authorizes every\n * gated request by it and the cookie it mirrors lives a year, so a URL carrying\n * it leaks that credential into browser history, the address bar, and every log\n * on the path. The landing is reached with a one-time grant instead — 256 bits\n * of entropy, a short TTL, and single-consume semantics — and the device id\n * reaches the client only inside the server-rendered shell (the capture script\n * the landing patches in).\n *\n * Consume semantics follow the reference implementation's one-time host\n * capability (zcode `packages/server/src/hostCapability.ts`): the record is\n * deleted on EVERY consume attempt — success, expiry, or replay — so a captured\n * grant is worthless after its first use and a replayed one can never resolve,\n * and only a first use inside the TTL yields a device.\n *\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui/pair-grant\n */\n\nimport { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'\n\n/**\n * Default grant lifetime. The grant only has to survive one redirect chain\n * from the accept page to the app landing, tunnel round trips included, so it\n * is far shorter than the device session it stands in for.\n */\nexport const DEFAULT_PAIR_GRANT_TTL_MS = 60_000\n\n/**\n * Cap on live grants. The accept page is rate-limited per source, but the\n * table is still caller-driven, so it stays bounded (oldest evicted first)\n * exactly like the device table.\n */\nexport const MAX_LIVE_GRANTS = 256\n\n/** Clock/entropy injection for tests. */\nexport interface PairGrantStoreOptions {\n  /** Grant lifetime in ms (default {@link DEFAULT_PAIR_GRANT_TTL_MS}). */\n  ttlMs?: number\n  /** Clock seam (default Date.now). */\n  now?: () => number\n  /** Entropy seam (default 32 random bytes, base64url). */\n  createGrant?: () => string\n}\n\n/** One issued grant and its absolute expiry (both non-secret to the issuer). */\nexport interface PairGrantRecord {\n  /** The one-time secret carried in the /pair-app URL. */\n  grant: string\n  /** Absolute expiry (ms epoch); a consume past this resolves to nothing. */\n  expiresAt: number\n}\n\n/** The grant table surface the routes consume. */\nexport interface PairGrantStore {\n  /** Mint one grant bound to a device session. */\n  issue(deviceId: string): PairGrantRecord\n  /** Redeem a grant once, returning its device id (undefined when unusable). */\n  consume(grant: string | undefined): string | undefined\n  /** Liveness check that does not spend the grant (the fence fallback). */\n  peek(grant: string | undefined): string | undefined\n  /** Live grant count (tests/diagnostics). */\n  readonly size: number\n}\n\n/** One live grant. */\ninterface GrantEntry {\n  deviceId: string\n  expiresAt: number\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the grant table. Pure TypeScript with injected clock/randomness so the\n * whole one-time semantics are unit-testable without a server.\n */\nexport function createPairGrantStore(options: PairGrantStoreOptions = {}): PairGrantStore {\n  const ttlMs = options.ttlMs ?? DEFAULT_PAIR_GRANT_TTL_MS\n  const now = options.now ?? ((): number => Date.now())\n  const createGrant = options.createGrant ?? ((): string => randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'))\n  const entries = new Map<string, GrantEntry>()\n\n  const purgeExpired = (at: number): void => {\n    for (const [grant, entry] of entries) {\n      if (entry.expiresAt <= at) entries.delete(grant)\n    }\n  }\n\n  return {\n    issue(deviceId: string): PairGrantRecord {\n      const issuedAt = now()\n      purgeExpired(issuedAt)\n      while (entries.size >= MAX_LIVE_GRANTS) {\n        const oldest = entries.keys().next().value\n        if (oldest === undefined) break\n        entries.delete(oldest)\n      }\n      const grant = createGrant()\n      const expiresAt = issuedAt + ttlMs\n      entries.set(grant, { deviceId, expiresAt })\n      return { grant, expiresAt }\n    },\n    consume(grant: string | undefined): string | undefined {\n      if (grant === undefined || grant === '') return undefined\n      const consumedAt = now()\n      const entry = entries.get(grant)\n      // Delete before validating: a replayed grant must never resolve, and an\n      // expired one must not linger in the table.\n      entries.delete(grant)\n      purgeExpired(consumedAt)\n      if (entry === undefined || entry.expiresAt <= consumedAt) return undefined\n      return entry.deviceId\n    },\n    peek(grant: string | undefined): string | undefined {\n      if (grant === undefined || grant === '') return undefined\n      const at = now()\n      const entry = entries.get(grant)\n      if (entry === undefined) return undefined\n      if (entry.expiresAt <= at) {\n        entries.delete(grant)\n        return undefined\n      }\n      return entry.deviceId\n    },\n    get size(): number {\n      return entries.size\n    },\n  }\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "packages/dsh-remote-web-ui/src/pairing.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Pairing state machine: one active one-time token, a device-session table,\n * and presence tracking. Pure TypeScript with injected clock/randomness so\n * the whole security semantics are unit-testable without cordis. The\n * cordis-facing surfaces (routes, the api/gate listener) live next door.\n *\n * Security invariants:\n * - One active token at a time; `issue()` replaces it, so a refreshed QR\n *   immediately invalidates the previous link.\n * - A token is a bearer credential for its whole window: it is refused only\n *   when unknown, expired, or after `stop()`, and the same link may pair\n *   repeatedly within that window (each accept mints a fresh device session).\n *   Mobile flows routinely split across cookie contexts (camera preview to\n *   in-app browser to the system browser), and the later context must be\n *   able to complete its own pairing from the same link.\n * - Tokens expire; `accept()` on an expired token is refused like an\n *   unknown one (no oracle for validity).\n * - `stop()` revokes every device session and clears the token, so paired\n *   devices are cut off on their next gated request.\n * - `revoke()` drops one device session; idle sessions older than\n *   `idleExpireMs` are deleted on sweep, load, and the next gated request.\n */\n\nimport { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'\nimport { mkdirSync, readFileSync, renameSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'\nimport { dirname } from 'node:path'\nimport type { PostureHost, PostureSnapshot } from './posture.ts'\nimport { sameIngressFrame, type IngressSyncFrame } from './ingress-sync.ts'\n\n/** The observable pairing phases the panel renders. */\nexport type PairingPhase =\n  /** The server is not bound all-interfaces: no usable QR exists. */\n  | 'lan-required'\n  /** Remote control was stopped; a fresh QR (issue) re-enables it. */\n  | 'stopped'\n  /** A token is live and no device has paired with it yet. */\n  | 'waiting'\n  /** At least one paired device was active recently. */\n  | 'connected'\n  /** Devices are paired but none has been active within the offline window. */\n  | 'disconnected'\n\n/** One issued pairing token (keyed by its secret). */\nexport interface TokenRecord {\n  /** Monotonic issue time (ms epoch), drives refresh ordering. */\n  issuedAt: number\n  /** Absolute expiry (ms epoch); accept() past this is refused. */\n  expiresAt: number\n  /** Opaque, non-secret identifier surfaced in snapshots (never the pairing secret). */\n  id: string\n  /** Workspace the QR link should land the phone in (optional). */\n  workspaceId?: string\n  /** LAN IP literal the QR link was built from (optional; default first). */\n  address?: string\n}\n\n/**\n * Default idle-expiry window: 30 days without a heartbeat or a gated\n * request. The reopen service worker refreshes lastSeenAt on every\n * navigation it serves, so the window only runs out through genuine\n * disuse; 30 days matches the browser-credential lifetimes the surrounding\n * flow was built around, while the effective device lifetime stays shorter\n * than the 365-day cookie because of this sweep. Override per deployment\n * through the idleExpireMs config.\n */\nexport const DEFAULT_IDLE_EXPIRE_MS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000\n\n/** Cap on the persisted/displayed User-Agent string. */\nconst MAX_USER_AGENT_CHARS = 180\n\n/** Cap on a user-defined device name. */\nconst MAX_DEVICE_NAME_CHARS = 64\n\n/** One paired device session, keyed by the device id stored in its cookie. */\nexport interface DeviceSession {\n  /** Pairing time (ms epoch). */\n  createdAt: number\n  /** Last time the device passed a gated request or heartbeat. */\n  lastSeenAt: number\n  /** Sanitized User-Agent captured at accept (optional; missing on old files). */\n  userAgent?: string\n  /**\n   * User-defined label shown instead of the User-Agent-derived name. Display\n   * metadata only: it is never read by an authorization decision, and a\n   * missing value keeps the derived-name fallback (optional; missing on old\n   * files).\n   */\n  name?: string\n}\n\n/** One device row in a loopback snapshot (ids are session credentials). */\nexport interface DeviceSnapshot {\n  /** Cookie value / session credential of this device. */\n  id: string\n  /** Pairing time (ms epoch). */\n  createdAt: number\n  /** Last heartbeat or gated request (ms epoch). */\n  lastSeenAt: number\n  /** Whether lastSeenAt is within the offline window. */\n  online: boolean\n  /** Sanitized User-Agent captured at accept, when known. */\n  userAgent?: string\n  /** User-defined label, when the operator renamed this device. */\n  name?: string\n}\n\n/** One tunnel status frame (auto-tunnel only; undefined when disabled). */\nexport interface TunnelStatus {\n  /** starting: binary/process warming up; running: URL minted; failed: no URL. */\n  state: 'starting' | 'running' | 'failed'\n  /** The minted public URL, once the tunnel reports it. */\n  url?: string\n  /** Human-readable failure detail. */\n  error?: string\n}\n\n/**\n * One relay-registry status frame (undefined while the stable-origin relay\n * is not in play: autoTunnel off, or the relay toggle disabled).\n */\nexport interface RelayStatus {\n  /** registering: a sync is in flight; running: the mapping is accepted. */\n  state: 'off' | 'registering' | 'running' | 'failed'\n  /** The stable relay origin (`https://<id>.dsh-market.com`). */\n  url?: string\n  /** Human-readable failure detail of the last sync attempt. */\n  error?: string\n}\n\n/** One snapshot frame pushed to desktop status streams. */\nexport interface PairingSnapshot {\n  phase: PairingPhase\n  /** Whether the server bind is all-interfaces (a QR is constructible). */\n  lanAvailable: boolean\n  /** The LAN IP literals a QR can be built from (interface order). */\n  lanAddresses: string[]\n  /** Configured public (tunneled) base URL, when present. */\n  publicUrl?: string\n  /** Auto-tunnel status, while the auto-tunnel feature is active. */\n  tunnel?: TunnelStatus\n  /** Relay-registry status, while the stable-origin relay is in play. */\n  relay?: RelayStatus\n  /**\n   * Update-only Cloudflare ingress sync status (issue #1948), once the feature\n   * has been enabled in this process. The public hostname, the local port and\n   * the two service strings are audit facts, not credentials.\n   */\n  ingress?: IngressSyncFrame\n  /** Latest /api posture probe (undefined until the first round completes). */\n  posture?: PostureSnapshot\n  /** Opaque (non-secret) id of the active token (undefined when stopped/lan-required). */\n  tokenId?: string\n  /** Absolute expiry of the active token. */\n  tokenExpiresAt?: number\n  /** Count of ever-paired devices. */\n  deviceCount: number\n  /** Count of devices active within the offline window. */\n  onlineCount: number\n  /** Per-device roster for the loopback panel (never sent on /api/pair/status). */\n  devices: DeviceSnapshot[]\n}\n\n/** Service tunables (config-validated upstream; plain numbers here). */\nexport interface PairingConfig {\n  /** Token lifetime; the QR stops working after this. */\n  tokenTtlMs: number\n  /** A device is \"online\" while its lastSeenAt is newer than this. */\n  offlineAfterMs: number\n  /** Hard cap on paired device sessions (oldest-evicted when full). */\n  maxDevices: number\n  /** Cookie name carrying the device id. */\n  cookieName: string\n  /**\n   * Idle sessions older than this are deleted (memory and disk). Defaults\n   * to {@link DEFAULT_IDLE_EXPIRE_MS} when omitted.\n   */\n  idleExpireMs?: number\n  /**\n   * Path to a JSON file where paired device sessions are persisted. When\n   * set, sessions survive process restarts (the phone keeps its 365-day\n   * cookie), so re-pairing after a dsh web restart is not required. When\n   * unset, sessions stay memory-only.\n   */\n  devicesFile?: string\n}\n\n/**\n * Result of one accept() attempt. A token is a bearer credential for its whole\n * window (see the module doc), so the only refusal is `invalid`: unknown,\n * expired, or after stop(). There is no \"already used\" outcome.\n */\nexport type AcceptResult =\n  | { ok: true; deviceId: string }\n  | { ok: false; code: 'invalid' }\n\n/**\n * Result of collapsing duplicate pairing records that one physical device\n * minted by pairing repeatedly. `not-duplicates` is a refusal, not a\n * no-op: the ids must name two or more live sessions sharing one User-Agent.\n */\nexport type MergeDevicesResult =\n  | { ok: true; deviceId: string }\n  | { ok: false; code: 'unknown-device' | 'not-duplicates' }\n\n/** Thrown by issue() for an address outside the sampled LAN literals. */\nexport class UnknownLanAddressError extends Error {\n  /**\n   * @param address - the offending literal.\n   */\n  constructor(address: string) {\n    super(`remote-web-ui: unknown LAN address ${JSON.stringify(address)}`)\n    this.name = 'UnknownLanAddressError'\n  }\n}\n\n/** Clock and entropy injection for tests. */\nexport interface PairingClock {\n  now(): number\n  randomToken(): string\n}\n\n/** File-operation seam for the revocation-durability step (tests). */\nexport interface PairingFsSeams {\n  /** Remove the stale device store (defaults to fs.rmSync with force). */\n  removeFile?(path: string): void\n}\n\n/** Real clock/entropy: 32 random hex chars per token. */\nexport const defaultClock: PairingClock = {\n  now: () => Date.now(),\n  randomToken: () => randomBytes(16).toString('hex'),\n}\n\n/**\n * The pairing state machine. Structural mutations issue/accept/stop/revoke\n * and config updates (LAN bases, tunnel, posture) notify state listeners\n * after the commit point that makes them true, and notification dedupes\n * against the last emitted snapshot.       "content": "/**\n * Relay control-plane client: the lease claim that turns one relay identity\n * into a lease row (the tunnel transports get a tunnel, its ingress, a CNAME\n * and the per-instance connector token; the bridge transport gets neither\n * block, because its data plane owns no Cloudflare object) plus the release\n * bookkeeping.\n *\n * Claiming is best-effort and additive. Every failure is graded into a retry\n * decision instead of breaking the quick tunnel that already serves the phone:\n * the control plane answers `mode`, so an instance whose claim cannot land\n * keeps the origin the registry gave it.\n */\n\nimport type { RelayIdentity } from './relay-registry.ts'\n\n/** The control-plane endpoints (market apex, never a relay hostname). */\nexport const RELAY_CLAIM_URL = 'https://dsh-market.com/api/relay/claim'\nexport const RELAY_RELEASE_URL = 'https://dsh-market.com/api/relay/release'\n\n/** Which connector serves the relay hostname. `bridge` is the Durable Object\n * meeting point (`relay-bridge-connector.ts`), `named` the instance's own cloud\n * tunnel, `quick` today's Worker proxy path. */\nexport type RelayConnectorMode = 'named' | 'quick' | 'bridge'\n\n/** What a bridge connector needs to dial: an endpoint and a credential to\n * present. The credential is the lease's own long-lived id and secret -- the\n * reply names it rather than repeating a secret in a body. */\nexport interface RelayBridgeGrant {\n  endpoint: string\n  instance: string\n  credential: 'lease-secret'\n}\n\n/** One accepted lease, as the control plane answers it. */\nexport interface RelayClaim {\n  mode: RelayConnectorMode\n  /** The instance's own tunnel. Absent for a bridged lease: there is nothing\n   * to run and no token to run it with. */\n  tunnel?: { id: string; token: string }\n  hostname: string\n  /** The CNAME target behind the hostname; absent for a bridged lease too. */\n  dns?: { target: string }\n  /** Present when the control plane can route this instance over the bridge. */\n  bridge?: RelayBridgeGrant\n}\n\n/** What one claim attempt resolved to. */\nexport type RelayClaimOutcome =\n  | { ok: true; claim: RelayClaim }\n  | { ok: false; status: number; error: string; retryAfterMs?: number }\n\n/** One claim request (the lease the caller wants refreshed). */\nexport interface RelayClaimRequest {\n  id: string\n  secret: string\n  /** Carried only by a fresh identity: the first claim creates the row. */\n  newSecret?: string\n  /** Local origin port the lease ingress points at (`ctx.webServer.port`). */\n  port: number\n  /** The plugin version, for the adoption readout of the migration. */\n  pluginVersion?: string\n}\n\n/** The capped backoff a failed claim retries on. */\nexport const CLAIM_RETRY_BASE_MS = 5_000\nexport const CLAIM_RETRY_MAX_MS = 60_000\n\n/** Build the claim body (an absent value is omitted, never sent as null). */\nexport function relayClaimBody(request: RelayClaimRequest): string {\n  return JSON.stringify({\n    id: request.id,\n    secret: request.secret,\n    new_secret: request.newSecret,\n    origin: { port: request.port },\n    plugin: request.pluginVersion === undefined ? undefined : { version: request.pluginVersion },\n  })\n}\n\n/** The tunnel of one accepted claim, or undefined when it carries none. */\nfunction relayTunnelOf(value: unknown): { id: string; token: string } | undefined {\n  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return undefined\n  const tunnel = value as { id?: unknown; token?: unknown }\n  if (typeof tunnel.id !== 'string' || tunnel.id === '') return undefined\n  if (typeof tunnel.token !== 'string' || tunnel.token === '') return undefined\n  return { id: tunnel.id, token: tunnel.token }\n}\n\n/** The CNAME target of one accepted claim, or undefined when it carries none. */\nfunction relayDnsTargetOf(value: unknown): string | undefined {\n  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return undefined\n  const target = (value as { target?: unknown }).target\n  return typeof target === 'string' && target !== '' ? target : undefined\n}\n\n/** One lease read back from an accepted claim, or undefined for a bad shape. */\nexport function relayClaimOf(value: unknown): RelayClaim | undefined {\n  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return undefined\n  const body = value as { mode?: unknown; tunnel?: unknown; hostname?: unknown; dns?: unknown; bridge?: unknown }\n  const mode = body.mode\n  if (mode !== 'named' && mode !== 'quick' && mode !== 'bridge') return undefined\n  if (typeof body.hostname !== 'string' || body.hostname === '') return undefined\n  const tunnel = relayTunnelOf(body.tunnel)\n  const target = relayDnsTargetOf(body.dns)\n  // The tunnel transports are served by that tunnel, so a reply without both\n  // halves is a protocol error. The bridge is the one transport whose lease\n  // owns no Cloudflare object, and its claim carries neither half.\n  if (mode !== 'bridge' && (tunnel === undefined || target === undefined)) return undefined\n  const bridge = relayBridgeGrantOf(body.bridge)\n  return {\n    mode,\n    ...(tunnel === undefined ? {} : { tunnel }),\n    hostname: body.hostname,\n    ...(target === undefined ? {} : { dns: { target } }),\n    ...(bridge === undefined ? {} : { bridge }),\n  }\n}\n\n/** The bridge grant of one accepted lease, or undefined when it carries none. */\nexport function relayBridgeGrantOf(value: unknown): RelayBridgeGrant | undefined {\n  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return undefined\n  const grant = value as { endpoint?: unknown; instance?: unknown; credential?: unknown }\n  if (typeof grant.endpoint !== 'string' || grant.endpoint === '') return undefined\n  if (typeof grant.instance !== 'string' || grant.instance === '') return undefined\n  if (grant.credential !== 'lease-secret') return undefined\n  return { endpoint: grant.endpoint, instance: grant.instance, credential: 'lease-secret' }\n}\n\n/** The error code and retry hint of a refused claim. */\nfunction refusalOf(status: number, detail: unknown): Extract<RelayClaimOutcome, { ok: false }> {\n  const body = typeof detail === 'object' && detail !== null\n    ? detail as { error?: unknown; retryAfterMs?: unknown }\n    : {}\n  const error = typeof body.error === 'string' ? body.error : 'http-' + String(status)\n  const retryAfterMs = typeof body.retryAfterMs === 'number' && Number.isFinite(body.retryAfterMs)\n    ? body.retryAfterMs\n    : undefined\n  return retryAfterMs === undefined ? { ok: false, status, error } : { ok: false, status, error, retryAfterMs }\n}\n\n/**\n * Claim one lease. A transport failure is graded like `502 cf-api-unavailable`\n * (status 0) so the caller retries on the same path as a refused upstream.\n * @param request - the lease to refresh.\n * @param options - endpoint and fetch seams (defaults are the real ones).\n */\nexport async function claimRelayLease(\n  request: RelayClaimRequest,\n  options: { url?: string; fetchFn?: typeof fetch } = {},\n): Promise<RelayClaimOutcome> {\n  const fetchFn = options.fetchFn ?? fetch\n  let response: Response\n  try {\n    response = await fetchFn(options.url ?? RELAY_CLAIM_URL, {\n      method: 'PUT',\n      headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\n      body: relayClaimBody(request),\n    })\n  } catch (error) {\n    const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)\n    return { ok: false, status: 0, error: detail === '' ? 'network-error' : detail }\n  }\n  const detail: unknown = await response.json().catch(() => undefined)\n  if (!response.ok) return refusalOf(response.status, detail)\n  const claim = relayClaimOf(detail)\n  return claim === undefined\n    ? { ok: false, status: response.status, error: 'invalid-response' }\n    : { ok: true, claim }\n}\n\n/**\n * Release one lease (the plugin's offline action: toggle off, profile\n * unmount). Best-effort — a release that never lands only leaves the row\n * marked active, which the 90-day GC recovers.\n */\nexport async function releaseRelayLease(\n  identity: RelayIdentity,\n  options: { url?: string; fetchFn?: typeof fetch } = {},\n): Promise<void> {\n  const fetchFn = options.fetchFn ?? fetch\n  await fetchFn(options.url ?? RELAY_RELEASE_URL, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({ id: identity.id, secret: identity.secret }),\n  })\n}\n\n/** How one failed claim should be retried. */\nexport interface RelayClaimRetry {\n  /** Whether another attempt is worth making at all. */\n  retry: boolean\n  /** How long to wait before that attempt. */\n  delayMs: number\n  /**\n   * Whether the identity must be re-claimed with `new_secret`: the control\n   * plane lost the row (a D1 restore or a manual wipe), which is the one\n   * condition a fresh claim fixes.\n   */\n  refreshIdentity: boolean\n}\n\n/**\n * Grade one failed claim into a retry decision.\n *\n * `403 auth-failed` is terminal: the id belongs to another secret and no\n * number of retries can take it back. Everything else retries on a capped\n * exponential backoff, with the control plane's own `retryAfterMs` (a 502\n * names it) raising the floor so a retry cannot land inside a known outage.\n * @param outcome - the refused attempt.\n * @param attempt - how many attempts already failed (0 for the first).\n * @param options - backoff bounds (defaults are the shipped ones).\n */\nexport function relayClaimRetryOf(\n  outcome: Extract<RelayClaimOutcome, { ok: false }>,\n  attempt: number,\n  options: { baseDelayMs?: number; maxDelayMs?: number } = {},\n): RelayClaimRetry {\n  const base = options.baseDelayMs ?? CLAIM_RETRY_BASE_MS\n  const max = options.maxDelayMs ?? CLAIM_RETRY_MAX_MS\n  if (outcome.status === 403) return { retry: false, delayMs: 0, refreshIdentity: false }\n  const backoff = Math.min(base * 2 ** attempt, max)\n  const delayMs = Math.min(Math.max(backoff, outcome.retryAfterMs ?? 0), max)\n  const refreshIdentity = outcome.error === 'invalid-params' || outcome.error === 'unknown-id'\n  return { retry: true, delayMs, refreshIdentity }\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * The remote desktop data channel: `/remote` is this plugin's own prefix, so\n * the paired-device cookie is the access control. After that gate, every\n * fenced same-origin path the browser rewrote here is re-issued to 127.0.0.1\n * as a loopback-shaped request so sibling plugin fences (and the connection\n * plugin's `/api`) accept it — no `--trusted-host` and no per-plugin pairing\n * consult.\n *\n * Security model:\n * - Every request must carry a live paired-device credential, enforced before\n *   any bytes are forwarded and before any host call. This gate is\n *   unconditional and does NOT follow `requirePairingForLan`: the channel\n *   re-issues traffic with the process's own browser-auth credential, so it is\n *   an authentication amplifier — an unpaired caller admitted here would reach\n *   the full host API without ever holding that credential. The LAN policy\n *   governs the plain `/api` surface only (whether the harness fence's LAN\n *   auto-trust stands on its own); it can never widen this channel.\n * - A paired remote desktop is a full-control credential: the browser half\n *   flips the official UI into host mode (the transport ownsHost hook), so\n *   the configuration plane (settings, credentials, presets, deliverables)\n *   rides this channel like every other call. The four control planes in\n *   LOCAL_ONLY_PREFIXES stay physically local.\n * - Everything else is HTTP- or WebSocket-proxied to the local port with\n *   Host rewritten, Origin and cookies dropped, and a synthetic same-origin\n *   browser marker added after authentication.
